scope: Different-author payload-free source hammer of the M1681 full-D0 8,700-shard execution closure. Synthetic fixtures test reachability, immutable FD/hash binding, namespace state, sealing, metric ledgers and reducer behavior. No canonical payload, replay, GPU, EDA or release was used.

p1.finding: verify_sealed_shard validates the result tree and attempt binding but does not require work/failure siblings to be absent. reduce_complete_sealed_shards calls it directly without first invoking resume_state. A synthetic result=true, attempt=true, work=false, failure=true state was accepted by verify_sealed_shard even though resume_state rejected the same state.
p1.impact: An ambiguous shard state can contribute to COMPLETE_8700_SEALED_SHARDS, so the reducer is not yet the claimed exact completion arbiter.
p1.required_repair: Require exact per-ordinal sibling topology {result:true, attempt:true, work:false, failure:false} in verify_sealed_shard or in the reducer before accepting each receipt, then add the reproduced attack as a permanent regression.

p2.finding: verify_sealed_shard checks attempt.exists and not symlink before hashing, but does not explicitly require a regular file with the source-created 0400 mode.
p2.disposition: Add a regular-file and mode check while repairing the P1. This is hardening because consume_attempt itself uses O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW and mode 0400, and receipt SHA binding rejects ordinary content drift.

single_next_action: Repair exact sibling namespace topology in the sealed-shard verifier/reducer and submit a fresh different-author source review. Do not create M1683.
